input:
## Basis
This report sets out the design of a distillation column intended to separate a key component from a process stream, and it documents the basis on which the sizing has been performed, the materials selected, and the principal risks that remain open at this stage. The design throughput is 58 t per day, and the separation duty specified for the column is the removal of 98% of the key component from the feed, a demanding target that drives much of what follows in this document. The feed is taken to enter the column as a saturated liquid at its boiling point, an assumption that simplifies the internal traffic calculations and is regarded as a reasonable starting point for a design at this level of definition, although it will of course need to be revisited if the upstream equipment delivers the feed in a different condition. Wetted parts throughout the column are specified in 316L stainless steel, a choice that is stated here in the basis and is not repeated elsewhere in the report. Design margins have been applied in the customary manner in order to accommodate the uncertainties inherent in a design developed from estimated physical properties, and the operating pressure has been selected with a view to keeping the temperatures within the column compatible with the available heating and cooling utilities on site.
## Sizing
The sizing of the column proceeds from the separation duty stated in the basis. The number of theoretical stages is estimated by standard shortcut methods in the first instance, and a tray efficiency is then applied in order to arrive at the number of actual trays that will be installed, since real trays do not achieve the full equilibrium separation that the theoretical picture assumes. The reflux ratio is chosen as a multiple of the minimum reflux ratio, and this choice involves an important trade-off, because a higher reflux ratio reduces the number of stages required but simultaneously increases the vapour and liquid traffic inside the column, the diameter that is needed to handle that traffic, and the duties imposed on the reboiler and the condenser at either end. The column diameter is set by the hydraulic capacity of the trays at the point of maximum vapour loading, with a prudent allowance below the flooding limit so that the column retains some tolerance for the inevitable fluctuations in feed rate and composition that arise in normal operation. The reboiler and condenser are sized from the internal traffic at the design reflux condition, and the resulting duties are passed to the utility systems for checking against the capacity actually available on site. The column height follows from the tray count and the tray spacing, together with the disengagement allowances required above the top tray and below the bottom tray for satisfactory operation. Nozzle sizes are selected from the line sizes of the connecting pipework, and the associated pressure drops are checked for consistency with the overall pressure balance of the system.
## Materials
The materials selection is governed principally by the corrosive character of the process fluid and by the temperatures and pressures encountered within the column. Wetted parts are executed in the stainless steel specified in the basis, which offers adequate resistance to the process environment across the full range of operating conditions envisaged, including the more aggressive conditions that can arise during start-up, shutdown and process upsets, when concentrations and temperatures may depart considerably from their normal values. Welds in wetted service are made with matching filler material and are subject to the inspection regime appropriate to pressure equipment, since a weld of inferior corrosion resistance would simply become the preferential site of attack and would defeat the purpose of the overall selection. Gaskets and other non-metallic components are chosen for compatibility with the process fluid at the design temperature, and bolting is selected to match the flange duty. External surfaces are protected against atmospheric corrosion by the site coating system, and insulation, where fitted, is provided with cladding arranged to shed water away from the shell. Materials for the column internals are matched to those of the shell in order to avoid galvanic couples in the presence of a conductive process liquid, and particular attention is paid to crevices at tray supports and attachment points, which are recognised sites for accelerated local attack in stagnant conditions.
## Risks
Two risks stand out as unresolved at the present stage of the design and are recorded here as open items rather than as matters that the design has settled. The first is fouling: the feed contains components with a tendency to deposit on trays and in the reboiler, and deposition would progressively degrade both the separation efficiency and the heat transfer, narrowing the operating window of the column over the course of a run. The rate of fouling cannot be predicted reliably from the data currently available, so the design neither credits a fouling allowance beyond normal margins nor proposes a cleaning regime, and the matter is left for resolution with operating experience and, if necessary, feed pretreatment. The second open item is turndown: the column is sized at the design throughput, and its behaviour at substantially reduced rates, where trays may weep and the separation deteriorate, has not been established. If the plant is expected to operate for extended periods well below the design rate, the tray selection and the control scheme will both need to be revisited, but no such requirement has been stated, and the report therefore leaves the turndown question open. Neither item is resolved in this report, and both should be carried forward into the next stage of design.
target:
## Basis
The column separates a key component from a liquid feed at a design throughput of 58 t per day, with a separation duty of 98% of the key component removed. Wetted parts are in 316L stainless steel; the material is specified here and not repeated in the sections that follow. The feed enters as a saturated liquid at its boiling point. The assumption fixes the internal traffic at its simplest distribution between the rectifying and stripping sections, and it holds only while the upstream equipment delivers the feed in that condition; a subcooled or partly vaporised feed changes the traffic and the stage requirement, and the design would be rechecked against the delivered condition. Operating pressure is chosen so that column temperatures suit the heating and cooling utilities available on site. Physical properties used in the sizing are estimated values, and the design margins stated in the sizing section absorb the uncertainty those estimates carry. The basis is a preliminary design basis: adequate for fixing the column size, the tray count and the exchanger duties, and not a substitute for sizing on measured property data. Feed composition is taken as the stated average composition across the operating campaign. The separation duty is set by the key component alone; the remaining components distribute between the two products as the equilibrium and the stage count dictate, and no specification is placed on them in this report. Where the feed composition moves away from the average, the product purities move with it, and the column as sized absorbs the movement through the reflux and boil-up adjustments available to the operator rather than through any change in the installed equipment.
## Sizing
Stage requirement is estimated first by shortcut methods, which return the minimum reflux ratio and the minimum stage count as the two bounds of the separation. The design reflux ratio is set as a multiple of the minimum. A ratio close to the minimum keeps the vapour traffic, the diameter and the reboiler and condenser duties small, at the cost of a tall column; a larger ratio buys fewer stages with larger traffic and larger duties. The multiple chosen is the compromise the design carries, stated so that the trade can be reopened if energy or capital costs move. A tray efficiency converts the theoretical stages into actual trays. The efficiency is an estimate for this system, and the tray count inherits its uncertainty; internals are therefore arranged so that trays can be added at the top and bottom of the column if commissioning shows the efficiency to be lower than assumed. Diameter is set by tray hydraulics at the section of maximum vapour loading, with the operating point held below the flooding limit by the stated margin, so that feed fluctuations within the normal band do not flood the column. Reboiler and condenser duties follow from the internal traffic at the design reflux condition and are passed to the utility systems for checking against site capacity. Height follows from tray count and tray spacing, with disengagement space above the top tray and a sump below the bottom tray. Nozzle sizes follow the connecting line sizes, and pressure drops are checked against the overall pressure balance. Control of the separation rests on the reflux flow and the reboiler duty, with the product draw rates held by level control in the reflux drum and the column base. The sizing leaves the control scheme workable across the normal operating band: the valves selected pass the design traffic with travel in reserve in both directions, and the column pressure is held by the condenser, so that a change in cooling duty does not disturb the stage temperatures beyond the band the separation tolerates.
## Materials
The stainless steel specified in the basis covers the shell, the trays and all wetted internals. Corrosion resistance, not strength, governs the selection: the process fluid attacks carbon steel at rates no corrosion allowance would accommodate, and the selected grade resists the fluid across the operating range, including the off-design conditions of start-up and upset, when concentrations and temperatures depart from their normal values. Welds in wetted service take matching filler and the inspection regime for pressure equipment, since a weld of lower resistance than the parent metal becomes the site of preferential attack. Gaskets are non-metallic and are selected for compatibility with the process fluid at the design temperature. Bolting matches the flange duty. Internals use the same grade as the shell, so that no galvanic couple forms between dissimilar metals in contact with a conductive liquid. Attachment points and tray supports are detailed to avoid crevices, which hold stagnant liquid and concentrate the attack. External surfaces take the site coating system, and insulation cladding is arranged to shed water clear of the shell, since corrosion under wet insulation proceeds out of sight.
## Risks
Fouling and turndown are open items. Neither is resolved in this report. Fouling: the feed carries components that deposit on trays and on reboiler surfaces, and deposition degrades separation efficiency and heat transfer as a run proceeds. No fouling rate can be predicted from the data available, so the design credits no fouling allowance beyond the stated margins and proposes no cleaning regime. The item closes with operating experience, or earlier if feed pretreatment is adopted. Turndown: the column is sized at the design throughput, and tray behaviour at substantially lower rates has not been established. Trays that weep at low liquid rates lose separation, and a column required to run for long periods well below the design rate would need a different tray selection and a revised control scheme. No turndown requirement has been stated, so the design carries none. Both items are carried into the next design stage as they stand: the fouling item with a request for feed deposit data, the turndown item with a request for a stated operating range. A third matter is recorded for completeness rather than as a risk of the same order: the sizing rests on estimated physical properties, and the stage count and duties will move if measured properties differ from the estimates. The margins stated in the sizing section are the allowance the design makes for that movement, and measured data, when available, replace the estimates without reopening the structure of the design.
